title_zh: 「管理期货」配置热潮：Andrew Beer（Dynamic Beta Investments）与 Nate Juresi（Novodeus Wealth Management）谈债券替代
subtitle_zh: 60/40 松动，债市风波当口，两位嘉宾解读管理期货 ETF 如何填补债券分散化角色。
summary_zh: 本期 ETF Edge 由 Dominic Chu 主持，对话 Dynamic Beta Investments 创始人兼管理合伙人 Andrew Beer 与 Novodeus Wealth Management 总裁 Nate Juresi，主题是管理期货（managed futures）配置热潮如何填补债券的分散化角色。Juresi 称固收是当下投资里最难的领域：收益率飙升让固收更有吸引力，但过去几年“抄利率顶”的投资者多半受挫，加之股债正相关性增强、长久期国债显著回撤，令投资者转向另类。Beer 提出战略资产配置与模型组合正面临存亡危机——2021 年底刚走出二十年最大债券泡沫时，人们仍因贴合 60/40 而加债券，是“配置的自杀”；他一直在为“史上最猛的一场债市风波（bond market tantrum）”做准备，认为财政支出失控而政客无意修复。他强调管理期货的价值远超其在组合中的体量：2022 年万物皆跌时该策略上涨约 20%，是“红色海洋里的一座绿色灯塔”，但必须打算持有穿越周期。两人谈到把 CTA、市场中性等对冲基金策略装进 ETF 外壳后更易触达，“降费是最纯粹的 alpha（超额收益）”，收益堆叠（return stacked）ETF 兴起，以及 BlackRock 去年 12 月推出、规模已近 80 亿美元的多量化多策略 ETF（代码 IALT）对高费率观念的正面强攻。是一集关于后 60/40 时代分散化工具的深谈。

turns.en: Welcome to ETF Edge, the podcast. If you're looking to learn the latest insights on all things exchange traded funds, you're in the right place. Every week we're bringing you compelling interviews, thoughtful market analysis and breaking down what it all means for investors.
turns.zh: 欢迎来到《ETF Edge》播客。如果你想了解关于交易所交易基金（ETF）的最新洞见，那你可来对地方了。我们每周都为你带来精彩的访谈、深入的市场分析，并为大家解读这一切对投资者意味着什么。

turns.en: I'm your host, Dominic Chu. Some investors are utilizing bonds in new ways right now and then adding a new tool or set of tools to fill the old roles of bonds. Here's my conversation with Andrew Beer, founder and managing member at Dynamic Beta Investments, alongside Nate Juresi, president of Novodeus Wealth Management.
turns.zh: 我是你们的主持人 Dominic Chu。眼下一些投资者正在以新的方式使用债券，并添补新的工具——或者说一组工具——来填补债券过去扮演的角色。下面是我与 Dynamic Beta Investments 创始人兼管理合伙人 Andrew Beer，以及 Novodeus Wealth Management 总裁 Nate Juresi 的对谈。

turns.en: Gentlemen, thank you very much for being here both with us right now for an ETF Edge that's going to tackle a little bit of the story around bonds and just what they've done and what role they play in a portfolio these days. And maybe Nate, I'll start with you on this one first.
turns.zh: 两位先生，非常感谢你们此刻做客《ETF Edge》。我们今天要聊一点债券的故事——它们一路走来表现如何，以及如今在组合里扮演什么角色。Nate，这个问题我想先从你开始。

turns.en: Have we seen any kind of opportunistic movement with regard to traders and investors to take advantage of some of these lower bond prices and higher yields, not just across the yield curve for treasuries, but also in corporate investment grade and high yield as well?
turns.zh: 我们看到交易员和投资者有没有什么机会性的动作，利用这波债券价格走低、收益率走高？不只是国债收益率曲线的各个期限，也包括投资级公司债和高收益债？

turns.en: There's no question. I think right now because of the environment where we have had yields surging, fixed income has become more attractive. That said, if you think back over the past several years, we've seen a lot of investors and traders attempt to top tick rates and that hasn't worked out very well. And so right now you have this interesting dynamic where fixed income investors are trying to figure out where they should be positioned along the yield curve. And it's a
turns.zh: 毫无疑问。我觉得当下在收益率飙升的环境下，固定收益变得更有吸引力了。话虽如此，回想过去几年，我们看到很多投资者和交易员想抄利率的顶，结果并不理想。所以现在出现了一个很有意思的局面：固收投资者正在琢磨自己该布局在收益率曲线的哪个位置。这是一个

turns.en: challenge. I call fixed income the most challenging area in investing right now. And I think that's one of the reasons why we're seeing investors look to alternatives outside of fixed income.
turns.zh: 挑战。我把固收称为眼下投资里最难的领域。我认为，这也是投资者开始寻找固收之外的另类选择的原因之一。

turns.en: So outside of fixed income, that's what we're going to turn to Andrew right now, because Andrew, one of the things that you look at, I mean, you look at a lot because you run funds that involve all kinds of different asset classes. I wonder from the bond perspective right now, if you've seen anything that indicates to you that we could be in for an opportunistic time to nibble on some of these lower prices or whether or not there is a chance that we could see even
turns.zh: 说到固收之外，我们接下来就问 Andrew。Andrew，你关注的东西很多——我是说很多，因为你管理的基金涉及各种各样的资产类别。我从债券的角度想问，眼下你有没有看到什么迹象，表明我们可能正处在一个可以逢低吸纳的机会窗口，还是说债市前方

turns.en: further downside for that bond market ahead? Well, sure. I think from our perspective, I mean, again, the strategy that we run are designed to be tactical. This has been a very, very good year to be tactical. What's driving inflation? What's driving the rise in bonds? Well, one thing is the rise in oil prices. This is a very good year to be buying crude oil in the 60s in January before the war starts. It's also been a great year to be betting on the rise in interest rates,
turns.zh: 还有进一步下跌的可能？嗯，当然会有。我觉得从我们的视角来看——再强调一次，我们运行的策略本身就是设计成战术性的。今年做战术操作非常、非常好。是什么在推动通胀？是什么在推动债券收益率上行？其中一个因素是油价上涨。今年一月份、战争爆发之前，在 60 多美元的价位买原油是很棒的。押注利率上升同样是极好的一年，

turns.en: which has been happening in recent months. So every investor out there will benefit, who has bonds in their portfolio, if rates start to come back down. But the challenge is what do you do when it's not working? And so in a sense, we've been positioned for what I would call the mother of all bond market tantrums. We have runaway fiscal spending. We have no appetite among politicians to fix it. And most investors are simply not able to capitalize on that in any
turns.zh: 过去几个月利率一直在涨。所以，凡是组合里有债券的投资者，只要利率开始回落都会受益。但难点在于：当它不起作用的时候，你怎么办？从某种意义上说，我们一直在为所谓“史上最猛的一场债市风波（bond market tantrum）”做准备。财政支出失控，政客们没有半点修复的意愿，而大多数投资者根本无法以任何

turns.en: meaningfully direct way. Now, could I follow up there by asking you then if it's the case where this bond tantrum is evolving and has gone a long way in a relatively short amount of time, those problems that you laid out are there not on a tactical level, but on a more secular level.
turns.zh: 有意义的方式直接加以利用。那我顺着问一下：如果这场债市风波正在演进，并且在相对短的时间里已经走了很远——你列出的那些问题，其实不在战术层面，而在更长期的趋势层面。

turns.en: These are things that are not fixed overnight. How exactly then do you see investors positioning for that rising rate environment and threat from things like geopolitics, oil prices because of it, and fiscal issues not just in the U.S., but around the world as well?
turns.zh: 这些东西不是一夜之间能解决的。那么你到底怎么看投资者为这种利率上行环境所做的布局——应对地缘政治、以及由此推高的油价，还有财政问题——不仅仅在美国，而是全世界？

turns.en: Well, I think broadly there's an existential crisis right now in strategic asset allocation and the model portfolio world. At the end of 2021, we've been talking about inflation coming back.
turns.zh: 嗯，我觉得从大方向看，战略资产配置和模型组合的世界现在正面临一场存亡危机。2021 年底的时候，我们一直在说通胀会卷土重来。

turns.en: We had come off two decades of the greatest bond bubble we'd ever seen. What did you do as an allocator at the end of 2021? You added bonds because your equities had gone up 28 percent, your bonds hadn't moved. It was allocation suicide from a capital allocation perspective, but people did it because they are constrained by this idea of we're going to match ourselves to 60-40 over time. What I've seen over the past several years is people saying we've got to rethink
turns.zh: 我们当时刚刚走出有史以来最大的债券泡沫——整整二十年。作为一个配置者，2021 年底你会怎么做？你会加债券，因为你的股票涨了 28%，而债券没动。从资产配置的角度看，这是配置的自杀，但人们还是这么做了，因为他们被“长期要贴合 60/40”这个想法束缚着。过去几年我看到的是，人们开始说：我们必须重新思考

turns.en: this. It is good to be tactical. It is good to have flexibility in your portfolio, but what we've done is we've conditioned an entire generation of investors that human beings, and they're absolutely right. Human beings are very, very bad at being tactical. They don't have all the tools that sophisticated hedge funds have to be able to capitalize on these kinds of opportunities.
turns.zh: 这件事。保持战术是好的，组合里有弹性是好的，但我们所做的，是让整整一代投资者形成条件反射——作为人类，而他们说得分毫不差——人类做战术操作是非常、非常差的。他们不像成熟的对冲基金那样，拥有捕捉这类机会的全部工具。

turns.en: So in a sense, what we've seen is people opening the mandate and saying, okay, bonds are there to serve a particular function, but so are many other different kinds of diversifiers, and how do we put that into a portfolio in a healthy, constructive way?
turns.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我们看到的是人们放宽了投资授权，说：好，债券是为了承担某种特定功能，但还有很多其他类型的分散化工具也是。我们如何把它们健康、有建设性地放进组合里？

turns.en: Now, let's go back to Nate for this one here. As somebody who allocates for a living and looks at all of these different types of opportunities, the 60-40 has been kind of like this paradigm, this construct tried and true for years at this point now. Is there any reason to believe that the bond side of things no longer acts the way it should or has in the past, and that is the reason why some investors are fretting what's going on right now with regard to interest rates and
turns.zh: 我们再回到 Nate。你是以配置为业的人，看遍各种机会。60/40 这么多年来一直是这种范式、一种久经考验的架构。有没有理由让我们相信，债券那一侧已经不再像过去那样发挥应有的作用——这也是为什么一些投资者对眼下利率等方面正在发生的事感到焦虑？

turns.en: everything else? Because we have seen a little bit more of a positive correlation or trading relationship between both stocks and bonds. Well, I think that's the challenge. I think Andrew hit the nail on the head and that the bottom line is that 40% of the portfolio has not worked very well over the past several years, and especially if you've extended duration, you've been in say 20-plus year treasuries, that's been a significant drawdown in that space,
turns.zh: 以及其他一切？因为我们看到股票和债券之间的正相关性——或者说联动关系——更强了一些。我觉得这正是难点。我认为 Andrew 说到点子上了：说到底，组合里那 40% 过去几年表现得并不好，尤其如果你拉长了久期，比如买了 20 年以上的长期国债，那块已经出现了显著的回撤，

turns.en: a huge detriment to a portfolio. The way that I think about this is that financial markets are always complex, but I think you can make the case that the current market environment is even more so, just given the uncertainty around whether AI will ultimately deliver on growth expectations that are currently baked in. As you mentioned, we still have sticky inflation.
turns.zh: 对组合是巨大的拖累。我是这么看这件事的：金融市场从来都是复杂的，但我认为眼下的环境尤其如此，光是 AI 最终能否兑现当前已被计入预期的增长，就充满不确定性。正如你提到的，通胀依然顽固。

turns.en: We have higher oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty. We've seen longer-term interest rates surging. There's a lot going on, and so when you have that type of environment, I think it has investors looking to alternatives, and certainly something like Managed Futures ETFs as a space where investors have turned their heads. Okay, so Managed Futures brings us back to you, Andrew, because you do run funds that are tied to Managed Futures and other alternative type
turns.zh: 油价更高，地缘政治不确定，长期利率一度飙升。要考量的东西太多了。所以在这样的环境下，我觉得投资者会把目光投向另类资产，像管理期货（Managed Futures）ETF 这个领域，确实成了大家扭头关注的方向。好，管理期货就把话题带回给你，Andrew，因为你管理的基金就挂钩管理期货和其他另类类型

turns.en: strategies typically used by more sophisticated investors and things like hedge fund products, commodity trading advisor-advised products, that sort of thing. So I guess maybe what I'm asking for an ETF manager who does these types of things, are you seeing a pickup and interest from people who would have maybe traditionally gone more towards bonds as a hedge against some of these issues, more towards these alternative type strategies,
turns.zh: 的策略，这些通常是更成熟的投资者用的——对冲基金产品、商品交易顾问（CTA）管理的产品，诸如此类。所以我想问的是，作为做这类事情的 ETF 管理人，你有没有看到兴趣在升温：那些原本更倾向于用债券对冲这些问题的人，正转向这些另类策略——

turns.en: which are not as well known to the investing public, but are gaining some ground these days for awareness? Absolutely, and what Nate says about the difficulty of this environment, I mean, it is an extraordinarily difficult investing environment, as we know. A few things are working, right? AI has been working spectacularly well. Most things are not, and what we're seeing, again, is an expanded view of, I mean, to back to some statistics on bonds, they've had a 55%
turns.zh: 这些策略对大众投资者来说没那么知名，但眼下的认知度确实在提升？完全正确。Nate 说的这个环境的难度，我深有同感——眼下的投资环境确实异常艰难，我们都知道。有几样东西在起作用，对吧？AI 表现得极其出色，大多数东西都不行。我们看到的是一种更开阔的视野——回到债券的一些统计数据：本十年债券与股票的

turns.en: correlation to equities this decade. They've returned less than cash with a 15% drawdown. It's been dead money for the entire decade, and every year there's a narrative about how this year is going to be great. 2023, bonds were supposed to come back. So I think what you're seeing broadly across the space is people saying, you know, we need things that do different things.
turns.zh: 相关性达到 55%，回报还不如现金，回撤 15%。整个十年都是死钱，而每年都有一个叙事，说今年债券会很棒。2023 年，大家还说债券会回来。所以我认为，整个行业普遍在形成一种共识：我们需要一些功能不同的东西。

turns.en: I fell in love with a strategy called Manage Futures, because tactical is really good, being nimble when other people aren't, and most allocators out there are simply frozen into very, very rigid constructs of how they should invest. I have bonds in my portfolio. I love my bonds, right? They give me quarterly coupons that drop into my bank account, and I'm very happy to see them. I'm not making it a 40% allocation for something that is not adding value to the rest
turns.zh: 我爱上了一种叫管理期货的策略，因为战术性真的很好——在别人做不到的时候保持灵活，而大多数配置者都被冻在非常、非常僵化的投资框架里。我自己组合里有债券，我很爱我的债券，对吧？它们每季度派息，直接落进我的银行账户，我很高兴看到它们。但我不会把 40% 配给一个对我组合其余部分

turns.en: of my portfolio. So we've seen a huge change over the past several years in terms of people saying there are other things that will do a much better job for us. And I say, don't ask me, ask Claude.
turns.zh: 没有增值作用的东西。所以过去几年我们看到了巨大变化，人们开始说：有别的工具能为我们做得更好。我说，别问我，去问 Claude。

turns.en: Go take your portfolio, put it into Claude, and say, show me how to make my portfolio better. I want liquidity. I like ETFs, various other criteria, and it will point you in the direction of things that'll help. All right. So Nate, if that's going to be the case, what exactly are people, investors, I guess, who want income? What do they do now? Because it's not necessarily that managed futures are the income-generating instrument that some people
turns.zh: 把你的组合拿进 Claude，说：帮我看看怎么让组合更好。我要流动性，我喜欢 ETF，还有各种其他条件——它会给你指出有帮助的方向。好。Nate，如果情况是这样，那么想要收入的投资者——我猜是追求票息的人——现在该怎么办？因为管理期货未必是有些人

turns.en: kind of are seeking. They're not there to give you that kind of quarterly paycheck. And these days, by the way, there are ETFs structured to give you even more frequent paychecks and that sort of thing. How is it that income investors are starting to reconcile their portfolios against this backdrop, where maybe these traditional income-producing assets are not producing the kind of income that they want or need? Well, like Andrew, I'm still a believer in bonds in a portfolio
turns.zh: 所寻找的那种创收工具，它不是用来给你发那种季度工资单的。而且顺带一提，如今有些 ETF 的结构甚至能给你更频繁的发薪。收入型投资者要如何在这个背景下重新校准自己的组合？当这些传统创收资产不再产生他们想要或需要的收入时，怎么办？我和 Andrew 一样，长期仍然相信债券在组合中

turns.en: longer term. Bonds clearly have a role, and as rates have come up, that's helped on the income side of the equation. But going back to managed futures, think about this. Year to date, an ETF like DBMF is up 20%. The S&P 500 is up around 15%. And then you look at aggregate bonds, they're negative. They're down over 2%. And so even for investors who are seeking income, when you see that negative total return, that's going to get your attention. And I think the
turns.zh: 的作用。债券显然有其角色，而利率上升之后，对收入这一侧是有帮助的。但回到管理期货这件事，你想：今年以来，像 DBMF 这样的 ETF 涨了 20%，标普 500 大约涨了 15%，而综合债券基金是负的，跌了超过 2%。所以，即便是追求收入的投资者，看到负的总回报，你也会警觉起来。我认为

turns.en: right answer here is alternatives maybe fit a sliver of the portfolio. They have a place, they fit in the sleeve of a well-diversified portfolio that includes stocks and bonds. But I don't think you just give up on the bond side of the equation. There's clearly income to be had there. And to me, it's just a balance. It's all about diversification. One of the things, Andrew, that you watch more closely is just how trends play out. And that's the reason why tactical
turns.zh: 正确的答案是：另类资产也许适合组合的一小部分。它们有位置，可以作为股票和债券构成的分散化组合里的一个条块（sleeve）。但我不认为你应该干脆放弃债券这一侧——那里显然还是有收入的。在我看来这就是一种平衡，一切都是分散化。Andrew，你盯得特别紧的一件事就是趋势如何展开，这也是为什么战术

turns.en: investing is kind of in your belly with these days. But being tactical and understating trends is something that a lot of investors have to kind of get their arms around. I'm not trying to say time the market, but they have to be a little bit more short-term in their thinking and a little bit more nimble with regard to how they get in and out of certain types of investments. How exactly are these types of products that are geared towards alternative investments that are more
turns.zh: 投资如今是你的看家本领。但既要有战术性、又要读懂趋势，是很多投资者需要慢慢掌握的。我不是说要择时，而是他们的思维要更短期一点，在进出某些类型的投资时要更灵活。那些面向另类投资、节奏更快、更具战术性的产品，

turns.en: fast-moving and tactical in nature? How is it that bringing them to the ETF wrapper has made them either more accessible or more understandable for people who want maybe a little bit of that diversification exposure, but don't fully understand what a commodity trading advisor does?
turns.zh: 把它们装进 ETF 外壳之后，是怎么变得更容易触达、或者更容易被理解的？尤其是那些想要一点分散化敞口、但并不完全了解商品交易顾问是干什么的人。

turns.en: So my job is to make the benefits of this space understandable to the broad population. Every allocator out there who wants to grow their assets over time, wants to sleep at night, is trying to improve their risk-adjusted returns. I believe that managers can help them to do that.
turns.zh: 所以我的工作，就是让大众理解这个领域的好处。每一个想长期让资产增值、想晚上睡得着觉的配置者，都在努力改善自己的风险调整后回报。我相信管理人能帮他们做到这一点。

turns.en: It's a hedge fund strategy. Going back to the idea of trends, all it is is tactical. You're trying to be early, contrarian, and right in the big things as they happen. If inflation is coming back, position for it. If war is going to break out in the Middle East, position for it. If there's a bond market tantrum, position for it. The rest of your portfolio will behave differently, but you want something that really does march to the beat of a different drum. What I think the space and
turns.zh: 它本质上是对冲基金策略。回到趋势这个概念——它讲的就是战术：在大事发生的时候，你要早、要逆向、而且要正确。通胀要回来了，就为它布局；中东要打仗了，就为它布局；债市要动荡了，就为它布局。你组合的其他部分会有不同的表现，但你要的就是一个真正按自己的鼓点走的东西。我认为这个行业——

turns.en: what we did essentially was to look at the space. These hedge funds have been doing it for a very, very long time and say, it's wonderful what they do, but God, it's expensive. We looked at it and basically said, maybe we can recreate what they do. What do technological innovations do? They
turns.zh: 我们所做的事情，本质上就是审视这个领域。这些对冲基金已经做了非常、非常久，然后说：他们做的事很棒，但天哪，太贵了。等你把执行成本、付给对冲基金管理人的费用全扣完，剩下的回报根本不够看。我们研究之后基本就是说：也许我们能复刻他们在做的事。技术创新是干什么的？它们

turns.en: make something cheaper, more attractive, have a better payoff profile for people at the end of the day. We basically looked at the space and said, maybe we can bring some sort of technological innovation to figure out the most important things that they're doing, synthesize it and do it in such a way that what people have said about us is one of the few ETFs where you can say we've beaten hedge funds at their own game, but it's because it's efficiency, which is in the blood of the ETF
turns.zh: 让东西更便宜、更有吸引力，最终给大家更好的回报结构。我们基本上就是看着这个行业说：也许我们能带来某种技术创新，找出他们做的最重要的事，把它合成起来，做成这样一种东西——人们对我们的评价是：这是极少数能说出“在对冲基金自己的主场打败了对冲基金”的 ETF 之一，而这靠的是效率，效率正是 ETF

turns.en: industry. Efficiency is a way to outperform over time. Can I follow up with that? Efficiency. How exactly do you garner that efficiency? How exactly do you then minimize the cost, frictions, certain tension points so that these products can be more retail focused for people who are more cognizant of things like that fee structure, especially in a market in ETFs where people focus on lower costs and implementation? A typical hedge fund in this space will often
turns.zh: 行业的基因。效率是实现长期跑赢的一种方式。我能顺着问一下吗？效率——你到底是怎么获得这种效率的？怎么把成本、摩擦、各种张力点降下来，让这些产品更面向零售、面向更在意这些东西的人——尤其是在 ETF 这个大家紧盯低成本和执行的市场里？这个领域典型的对冲基金常常

turns.en: trade hundreds of sometimes very, very obscure contracts, things you would never normally think about as having an impact on a portfolio. They do it because their job is to analyze the world in all of its complexity to see signs that things are changing here and signs that are changing there. When they implement their portfolios, they implement them with a similar level of complexity, getting in and out of these markets trades all the time. When we looked at the space, I said,
turns.zh: 交易几百个有时非常非常冷门的合约——你根本不会想到它们会影响一个组合。他们这么做，是因为他们的工作就是分析这个极其复杂的世界，寻找这里那里正在变化的信号。他们构建组合时也用同样复杂的程度，在这些市场里不断进出交易。而我们审视这个行业的时候，我说：

turns.en: if I give you $100, you're going to turn over my portfolio 25 or 30 times during the course of the year. For me as a longtime hedge fund guy, that is staggeringly inefficient when what I really care about is inflation coming back. Is the dollar getting stronger? Are equities going to keep going up or keep going down? What we found was a way to basically synthesize these very, very complicated portfolios into 10 major markets. You can see that every day. We can put it into an ETF,
turns.zh: 如果我给你 100 美元，你一年里会把我的组合换手 25 到 30 遍。对我这个干了很久的对冲基金的人来说，这低效得惊人——而我在乎的其实是：通胀在回来吗？美元在走强吗？股票还会继续涨还是会继续跌？我们发现的办法，是把这些极其复杂的组合合成为 10 个主要市场。你每天都能看到。我们可以把它装进 ETF，

turns.en: you can see our positions every single day. What we found was that actually we could generate as good or better returns than we of the hedge funds in the space, but because we could save maybe 300 or 400 basis points on the implementation side, and it wasn't just that. I wanted to set up an ETF that was not competing with Vanguard at five basis points, but was still
turns.zh: 你每天都能看到我们的持仓。我们发现，实际上我们能创造与业内对冲基金相当甚至更好的回报，而且因为我们在执行端能省下大约 300 到 400 个基点。还不止这些，还有对冲基金的收费——这个领域的对冲基金一年要收两三百个基点。我想做的 ETF 不是去跟 5 个基点的 Vanguard 竞争，

turns.en: unbelievably attractive relative to the mutual funds in hedge funds in space. turns.zh: 而是相对同类的共同基金和对冲基金仍然有惊人的吸引力。我们有句话：降费是最纯粹的 alpha（超额收益）。这有点技术流，但如果你能压低一个投资策略的成本，把更多好处返还给客户，久而久之你就会有一支非常满意、非常忠实的客户群。这就是我们在做的。有意思。Nate，如果我们能更高效地使用这些策略，

turns.zh: 那个 60/40 了。你到底怎么做资产配置？对你服务的客户来说——我理解每个人的配置都不同，人生阶段不同、目标不同、风险画像不同——但当年的 60/40，60% 股票加 40% 债券，本来也不是适合所有人，只是变成了一个非常一刀切的模板。在如今这些新投资工具面前，特别是跟踪另类策略的 ETF、

turns.en: for things like ETFs that track alternative strategies, managed futures and the like? Andrew was talking about the benefits of the ETF wrapper. When you think about the cost efficiencies involved with that, I'll add something else, which is that we talked earlier about how complex the current market
turns.zh: 管理期货之类，这种格局发生了什么变化？对我来说，一切还是要回到教育，回到理解底层投资在更大组合里是怎么发挥作用的。我接一下刚才的话头。Andrew 说了 ETF 外壳的好处，讲到其中的成本效率，我再补一点：我们前面谈到现在市场

turns.zh: 而像 DBMF 这样的策略，可以移除这种情绪，因为它们是量化、系统化的策略，把人的情绪和偏见从方程里拿掉。再往外看一层：即便你作为投资者或顾问来配置这些策略，底层的情绪已经被从策略里拿掉了，你自己也得管住手，让这些策略穿越完整的市场周期去发挥作用。
